r0273 · criteria v2Nov 21, 09:29 EST

  • revision reason: Implement the originally recorded minimum lift duration with its earliest satisfying row, allowing uninterrupted ordered turn and carry as described in the demonstration. No thresholds change.
  • 7688 characters of criteria text
Criteria text

Plug manipulation verification

This evaluation uses the single white plug in the deployment layout. Starts span the specified ±10 mm in each planar coordinate and ±10° in blade heading around −90°, with its state +X up. The skill is a right-handed pickup, airborne finger-driven turn, leftward carry, supported set-down and release. The left side means the station goal zone.

Evidence from the demonstration

The reference is reconstruction version 5, record r0007. The white plug governs the deployment criteria. The second pickup corroborates the finger-driven turn. Video frames below use 30 fps.

Phase of the white plugFramesVideo and reconstruction evidence
Approach and enclosure27–104The right hand approaches from near-right with its palm facing the desk. The thumb closes on one housing side and other digits approach the opposite side. The housing stays supported. The median downward palm component over the first twelve annotated contact frames is 1.00.
Lift and turn105–142The pinch lifts the housing and the blades emerge as the fingers change shape. The longest geometrically opposed, clear interval spans 1.83 s. The maximum bottom clearance is 48.5 mm. Over that interval the blade direction changes by up to 69.6° relative to the wrist and the wrist orientation changes by 42.2°. The video shows the pinch changing shape through the turn, with some views of the contact occluded.
Carry and lower143–177The hand tracks the plug to the left, with the blades turned toward the vertical, then lowers it onto its base. Net demonstrated centre displacement is 205.6 mm toward +Y.
Steady and release178–223The fingers come away and the plug remains supported, blades pointing up. The fitted final supported pose has 0° blade tilt. The video shows the white plug standing through the second pickup.

The table and calibration set the metric scale. Blade direction and motion of the wrist are reconstructed in 3D. Frames 126–135 provide a specific turn witness. The relative blade direction changes 47.7° as its tilt moves from 56.2° to 24.3° from vertical, with 12.1° of wrist rotation. Exact pad locations and forces under occlusion remain inferred. Geometric opposition in the demonstration audit means a thumb and another finger within 5 mm of the model surface with directions at least 60° apart around its centre. The evaluation uses the robot's simulated contacts and encoders.

Ordered checks

A drop or missed grasp may be followed by another complete attempt. Lifting and onset of turning may overlap. The plug stays supported by the hand through the qualifying turn and into the carry. The evaluator logs the complete episode and uses the measured palm pose.

The lift is established at the first logged row with at least 0.13 seconds of uninterrupted qualifying clearance since the interval began. The turn may finish at or after this row while the same grip continues into carry. The first implementation looked for the end of the entire clearance interval. This timing correction implements the minimum duration stated in version 1 and preserves each stage threshold and the required order. The r0238 montage for seed 903955589 shows the plug remaining aloft through several seconds of in-hand motion, before a drop that still fails the turn and carry checks. The independent continuous-grip timing regression and broken-grip controls are recorded in research/simulation/lift_timing_regression.json.

  1. lift. The thumb and another finger contact the object on opposed sides, with the two contact directions at least 60° apart around the housing centre. The lowest point of the plug clears the tabletop by at least 10 mm continuously for 0.13 s, free of the environment. The palm-side normal, palm +X, has a downward component of at least 0.30 at the qualifying lift. The clearance is below the demonstrated 48.5 mm and distinguishes the lift from contact tolerance. The 0.13 s window covers four 30 Hz periods. The downward cone accommodates the two hands' different geometry. Use 15 mm of centre rise as an independent lift check. The reconstructed centre rises 60.3 mm. Standard checks are max_rise_m ≥ 0.015 and opposed_s ≥ 0.13.
  2. finger_turn. Within one clear opposed grip, the blade direction rotates at least 45° relative to the palm while the blade axis moves from at least 55° to at most 25° from vertical. Measure the angle between the object's +Z axes expressed in the measured palm frame at the two endpoints. The palm orientation may change up to 50° during that window and its +X normal must retain a downward component of at least 0.30 across at least 80% of the window. The clip's strongest relative blade turn is 69.6° and the observed grip phase remains palm-down. The tolerance accommodates different finger lengths, reach and the fitted angle's uncertainty. The standard passive-rotation proxy treats a 100 ms window with combined finger encoder change below 0.30 rad/s as passive. Allow at most 20° cumulative passive relative rotation in the qualifying turn and in the episode's opposed intervals. This allows brief settling while most of the 45° minimum turn remains active. Standard checks are opposed_rel_rotation_deg ≥ 45, opposed_object_rotation_deg ≥ 45 and passive_rel_rotation_deg ≤ 20. The blade-direction measurement is invariant to the 180° housing-axis symmetry.
  3. carry. After the turn, keep the plug in hand and move it left into the station goal rectangle while the entire plug remains at least 8 mm clear of the tabletop and blades are within 35° of up. Hold that condition continuously for 0.10 s before table contact. The clip moves 205.6 mm toward +Y and shows the blades remaining near up through the carry. The carry cone allows modest inclinations while the plug is held. Standard check is held_s ≥ 0.23, covering the minimum lift and carry windows together.
  4. placed. Set the plug on the flat housing end in the goal zone, release it, and have the hand clear and at rest to the end. Apply the full condition below. Standard predicates check the final centre limits, final +Z angle and absence of hand contact in the final row. The evaluator checks the same limits, velocities and robot rest over the entire last 0.5 s. The standing height for the specified 43 mm housing at a tabletop height of −0.315 m is −0.2935 m.
Success condition (given; include it unchanged in your criteria):
- the plug's body centre is in the goal zone, x in [0.28, 0.48] m and y in [-0.10, 0.05] m;
- it stands blades up: its +Z axis is within 10 deg of vertical;
- its centre is at its standing height on the table within +-10 mm;
- it is at rest: linear speed below 0.02 m/s and angular speed below 0.5 rad/s;
- all of this holds over the last 0.5 s of the episode, and the hand does not touch it then;
- the robot is at rest then too: over the same 0.5 s every finger joint moves less than 0.05 rad (max - min of its encoder reading) and the palm less than 5 mm.

An episode succeeds when every stage passes, the hardware is within its limits, and no stop ends it. At least 80% of independent deployment starts must succeed in the task suite, with zero hardware violations. This is the specified mastery rate and requires reliable completion across the full starts and sensor conditions. The feasibility suite uses the same starts and stage checks with the specified 25% pass rate for its existence proof. Target trials provide video and estimated poses. The judgment uses visible evidence for the same events, with 3D contact and force treated as uncertain where they cannot be resolved from the target views.

Limitations
list (8 items)Target finger torque/block geometry and glove properties remain to be calibrated., Articulated position projection uses published arm response without a full motor and gearbox inertial model., The 59 g estimate comes from a dimensionally similar Apple unit. Mass and friction are uncertain., Replays and independent gate tests are required for physical contact and behavior., The main contact stiffness has been calibrated to limit gross interpenetration. Its real physical value remains unknown., Proprioceptive delay takes values on the 100 Hz clock relative to each 30 Hz call. The quantization error is at most 5 ms away from the episode boundary., The blocked-index fixture retains its drift warning. These calibrated model values are physical priors., The v4 and continuous-arm model can differ during high-force grip changes. GPU planners provide proposals whose outcomes are accepted only after exact continuous-arm CPU replay. The known model divergences remain relevant to transfer.

GPU planners provide proposals whose outcomes are accepted only after exact continuous-arm CPU replay. The known model divergences remain relevant to transfer.

list (6 items)Target finger torque/block geometry and glove properties remain to be calibrated., Articulated position projection uses published arm response without a full motor and gearbox inertial model., The 59 g estimate comes from a dimensionally similar Apple unit. Mass and friction are uncertain., Replays and independent gate tests are required for physical contact and behavior., The main contact stiffness has been calibrated to limit gross interpenetration. Its real physical value remains unknown., The actual glove thickness and loaded friction between fingers are unmeasured. Convex hulls approximate the adjacent distal link shapes, and the exact flat-table blocked-index fixture departure persists.

In the exact flat-table scenario the index mcp1 saturates during the initial block. The lateral mcp2 also saturates, allowing the glove to slide sideways while the wrist yields under contact. The fingertip moves along the tabletop and ultimately reaches the close target. The measured final mcp1 gap and capped sustained torque tests fail. No stop is invented. The full geometry exposes a different contact mode than the fixture assumption, and long training will require resolving this calibration discrepancy.

Hypotheses, decisions, reflections and blockers.

hypothesisSeparate persistent bias from fresh exploration. Reuse the exact 96 physical and sensor starts and ordinary turn-scale c1688 branch recorded in r0610 as a paired control. Keep Gaussian step…

Separate persistent bias from fresh exploration. Reuse the exact 96 physical and sensor starts and ordinary turn-scale c1688 branch recorded in r0610 as a paired control. Keep Gaussian step innovation at 0.12 and pickup scale at 0.33, set only the recorded per-episode Gaussian bias multiplier from one to zero, and keep the RNG draws in sequence. Require at least six new full safe exact turns, no added safety events and at most two lost lifts. If it passes, repeat on a fresh 96 before proposing PPO. The preceding established-turn noise reduction did not qualify.
 · r0614 · Nov 21, 17:06 EST
decisionThe increased coverage integration completes 24 exact PPO updates and 9,216 sampled calls with the proposed reset mix and the matched policy interface. Forty episodes finish, including four true full…

The increased coverage integration completes 24 exact PPO updates and 9,216 sampled calls with the proposed reset mix and the matched policy interface. Forty episodes finish, including four true full starts and four checked live turn resets. Two are after a real completed turn and one advances a new held 10 mm. No limit violation, contract event or failed restoration. The seven monitored arm collisions are in one lifted reset, two cold carry resets and four cold release resets, with the same physical stop rules. The exact 105-minute comparison is now queued behind the c1688 bridge processes, whose scheduled endpoint is about 22:22 UTC.
 · r0613 · Nov 21, 17:05 EST

Preregister the next 105-minute matched exact PPO pair after the c1688 bridge trainers end. Logged mode-three calls on recent turn studies occupy 2.5 to 6.5 percent of sampled steps. Hypothesis: more coverage of physically valid before/after contexts extends safe held motion while retaining deployment pickup. Both use c1688 PPO weights, critic and Adam with LR 0.00010, seed 77262043, eight exact CPU workers each on CUDA2 and CUDA3, the same 43-source c0280 pre/post pool, standard transfer reward, mechanics, bounded decoder, one-third pickup and anchored-turn exploration, and pickup screening. The only difference is moving 20 percentage points of initial pregrasp reset probability into the turn pool, with deployment 29 percent unchanged. The variant mix is 29,7,14,30,10,10 percent. Fixed assessments at ages 10,34,66 and 102 minutes use ordinary full64, held early/low/release panels, earlier-turn12 and independent post-turn15. At 34 minutes, stop an arm with fewer than two safe exact nominal turns, zero safe same-grip upright held goals, fewer than six verified independent post-turn 10 mm advances and fewer than three truly new advances on earlier-turn holdout origins. A gate candidate needs independent nominal turn gain and safety and earlier-stage retention. Record realized turn call share as well as reset frequency.

The terminal height c1440 checkpoint reaches upright held goal dwell on 25 of 48 fresh assisted reset indices. In a paired exact continuation only two out of 25 ordinary arrivals and one out of 25 with frame-190 wrist preparation plus the same descent bias remain safe for a full episode. Four prepared paths across three physical origins touch down before running into a later physical arm collision, so none is a safe continuous touchdown or placement. First held goal Link7 margin ranges from −106.36 to +7.92 mm. This convinces me the assist does not transfer with safety in the terminal height actor; retain the earlier matched Link7 plan. The probe is diagnostic only and contributes no action labels or reset states.

Close both preflights without a policy change. On 96 full nominal c1688 starts per condition, ordinary and one-third established turn noise each give 91 safe lifts and zero exact turns or 10 mm held transport. Median opposed hold grows from 1.20 to 1.99 s but safety events rise from four to five. For housing geometry, all 172 restored suffix trials stay safe. At ordinary post-turn noise 0.12, only two distinct sources lower a contact 3 mm while keeping the grip, and one does so on both draws. At 0.04 there are two distinct sources and none on both draws. This misses the recorded six- and two-source threshold, so do not train the signed housing-support penalty at scale. Next test more ordinary PPO coverage of the existing physical turn contexts, which currently account for only 2.5 to 6.5 percent of recorded calls despite supplying verified held transport.
 · r0610 · Nov 21, 17:02 EST
hypothesisRequire ordinary PPO exploration to show physical reachability before a full carried-housing support study. On the distinct 43 training-only restored post-turn states, compare two independent samples…
more
Require ordinary PPO exploration to show physical reachability before a full carried-housing support study. On the distinct 43 training-only restored post-turn states, compare two independent samples each at raw random scales 0.04 and 0.12, with c1688 actions after the exact c0280 prefixes and no assistance. Seek a 3 mm reduction in the blade-axis location of at least one opposing real contact without interruption, on at least six safe distinct sources at 0.12, including two sources where both draws improve. If met, test only the signed housing cost against turn-continuation control with matched c1688 PPO weights, optimization, context pool and plant. I opened both r0014 failure montages. Both show the plug between thumb and opposing pads at 2.50 s, then briefly airborne below the hand at about 5.22 s as the fingers separate during the turn. Gate r0014 counted 26 of 32 lifts and no turn or placement. The gate reported 15 hardware violations and two torque halts. Replays of the halted seeds locate the largest torque during the empty-hand descent, at 7.79 s (-21.97 Nm) and 8.05 s (-38.97 Nm). Independent traces also show early mcp2 load at pickup and a later overrun in a wrong empty-hand deposit path. Enforce a measured grip before continuing to deposit, and maintain inward contact through the pivot using actual contact geometry. Variation across grip scale explains why the varied-start gate lifted more reliably than our nominal screen.
